question.text: What is 'tipping off' in the context of suspicious transaction reporting?

answer.text: Informing a customer or any third party that a Suspicious Transaction Report has been or will be filed about them
Providing a tip to law enforcement about a potential money laundering case
Sharing confidential client information with other financial institutions
Reporting unusually large transactions to the branch manager

explanation.text: The Logic: Tipping off is the prohibited disclosure that a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) or related information is being reported or provided to FIU-IND. The client must not be told of the report or the underlying suspicion before, during, or after STR submission. The Trap: "Providing a tip to law enforcement" is the opposite of tipping off — reporting to FIU-IND is the obligation under the PML framework, while tipping off the subject of the STR is what is prohibited. Note: The prohibition on tipping off, and the no-disclosure-to-the-client rule before, during, or after STR submission, are grounded in the checked Series XXIV workbook pages.
